sections.content: There are two polite ways to order. *Kérek* means “I would like” in the everyday way and fits cafés, shops and friends: *Kérek egy kávét.* *Szeretnék* is a little softer and more polite: *Szeretnék egy teát.* Learn *szeretnék* as one ready-made phrase; do not change its ending yet.

sections.title: Two ways to order
rows: Everyday: I would like a coffee.
Softer, more polite: I would like a tea.

sections.title: The -t after both
sections.content: The thing you order is the object after both, so it takes *-t*: *kávét*, *teát*, *süteményt* (cake), *szendvicset* (sandwich). With *egy* + container the food gets the *-t*: *Kérek egy pohár vizet.*

items.english: I would like two glasses of water.
I would like a piece of cake.

sections.content: Both are about you (*én*). To ask a friend, use another form of *kér*, on the next screen.
